findings.specText: story-051 Overview item 2: "**ycn20l24 — sync before sizing the zap.** `pool()` calls `pair.sync()` before reading reserves ..." (also checklist: "Write a failing unit test reproducing ycn20l24")
findings.specSource: story-051 document (review); repeated in the 267660b commit body ("ycn20l24: pool() syncs the pair..."), test/UniPoolerV2.t.sol section header "Story 051 — ycn20l24", and the test/UniPoolerV2.fork.t.sol docstring "ycn20l24 on the real pair"
findings.actualBehavior: In the ledger, ycn20l24 is L-24 (8511fd5206, wont-fix): the constructor checks only the pair's token set and not that it is the factory's canonical pair, plus the dust pre-seed grief. The sync finding is ycn20l25 / L-25 (8ec2be7d59, fix-pending). So the story, the commit and the tests credit the sync fix to a wont-fix entry. The canonical-pair change (#3), which does remediate the non-canonical-decoupling half of the real L-24, carries no label at all.
findings.deviation: Spec/commit labels do not match the ledger. This creates a reconciliation hazard: a label-driven closer could close L-24 (wont-fix, only half addressed: the dust pre-seed half is untouched) and leave L-25 (actually fixed) open, or the reverse.
findings.recommendation: Use fingerprints, not issueIds, to reconcile. Propose L-25 8ec2be7d -> fixed at 267660b (a human applies it; the fix is verified by mutation and fork tests). Annotate L-24 8511fd5206 that its canonical-pair half landed in 267660b while the dust pre-seed half stays wont-fix. Correct the label in story-051 (product-owner), or record the alias in the ledger note.

findings.specText: NatSpec :56-59: "V2 `swap()` credits the input as `balance - reserve`, so tokens transferred to the pair without a sync (a donation) would be absorbed into our swap and LP mint"; :60-62: "Syncing folds the donation into the reserves — to the pair's LPs, overwhelmingly this contract's POL". story-051 Background: "any unsynced balance in the pair is credited to our swap/mint by the real pair maths"; Implementation Notes: "(to the LPs, overwhelmingly the protocol)"
findings.specSource: UniPoolerV2.sol NatSpec at 267660b + story-051 document (Background, Change 2 notes)
findings.actualBehavior: Without a sync, the router fixes amountOut from the stale reserves. The donation only enlarges swap()'s computed amountIn, which loosens the K check, and swap()'s _update() then folds it into the reserves. The pooler receives nothing extra from the swap or the mint. The stranding comes from the router's _addLiquidity quoting against the shifted post-swap reserves while s was sized on the stale ones. In both cases (unsynced pre-fix, and synced post-fix) the donation accrues pro-rata to the LP holders that existed before our mint. Because mainnet V2 feeTo is ON (0xf385...5f85) and sync() does not touch kLast, feeTo also takes about 1/6 of the sqrt(k) growth the donation causes at the next mint/burn, our own addLiquidity included. 'Overwhelmingly this contract's POL' holds only to the extent that UniPoolerV2 holds the pre-existing LP. The cutover seed LP recipient is set by the phStaging2 script, not this contract.
findings.deviation: Comment and story premise only. Code behaviour is correct, and the fix (sync before sizing) is the right one under either description. The quotePool NatSpec claim that 'when [the fee] is on ... only raises our LP' was checked and holds: the fork test passes with LP >= quote on the real feeTo-on pair.
findings.recommendation: Reword the NatSpec as: 'without a sync, a donation is folded into reserves by swap()'s _update after s was sized on the stale reserves, so addLiquidity's optimal-amount selection no longer matches the two legs. Syncing first folds it before sizing. Either way the donation accrues pro-rata to existing LP holders (and to feeTo's protocol-fee share).'

findings.subtype: spec-supersession (implicit waiver of story-048 verbatim clause)
findings.specText: story-048: "The mint path (`_dispatch`) is kept verbatim, so the NFT minter, the mint-debt hook and NFT index 4 all see an identical dispatcher."; Plan §4 Stage 1a: "The `_dispatch` override copied **verbatim**"; "**Kept verbatim.** `_dispatch`, `_psmDonate`, ..."
findings.actualBehavior: With comments stripped, _dispatch differs from BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch by exactly one statement: `if (address(hook) == _defaultHook) revert UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet();`. _psmDonate differs only in revert-string prefixes. An un-hooked UniPoolerV2 now reverts every index-4 mint, where BalancerPoolerV2 would silently accrue zero debt, so 'identical dispatcher' no longer holds until setHook is called. The contract @dev header was reworded honestly (story-051 Autonomous Decision 8).
findings.deviation: Story-048's verbatim/identical-dispatcher clause is superseded by story-051, which explicitly mandates the guard as the first line of UniPoolerV2._dispatch. The later, owner-directed spec wins, so this is not a Law-2 violation of the code. But story-051 never states that it waives 048's clause, and the 048 document still asserts it. A reader grading against 048 alone would raise a false deviation.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line supersession note to story-048 (or 051): 'the _dispatch verbatim clause is amended by story-051: the hook-not-set guard is the only behavioural difference'. No code change.

notes: sync() before sizing: sync is permissionless on the pair, so calling it adds no capability an attacker lacked. A donation-based front-run costs the attacker the donation (it accrues to LPs), and its price effect is bounded by minPhusdOut/minLP exactly as a swap front-run is (L-22, wont-fix, unchanged).

Hook guard: it adds only reverts, and only in the un-hooked state. Cross-repo callers (phoenix-nft-staking BatchNFTMinter:287 and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken:650) mint a single fixed index, so an un-hooked index 4 fails loudly as intended. No multi-index loop gets bricked. The bypass via a fresh DefaultDispatchHook is a knowing owner action (Law 3).

Canonical-pair binding: it removes the non-canonical decoupling vector. Operational note (not a finding, given L-24 wont-fix context): the new pair_ NatSpec prescribes 'the pair is created first, the pooler deployed, then the pair seeded'. The constructor equally accepts a pair that is already seeded, so the protocol could create and seed atomically via Router02.addLiquidity (which creates the pair) before deploying. That would avoid an exposed empty canonical pair between createPair and seed, the L-24 dust pre-seed window. The ordering is a phStaging2 script concern (stories 100/101/103).

Pre-seed edge: a pair with balances on both sides but totalSupply==0 (donated, then synced by anyone) makes quotePool return expectedLP=0. That state was already reachable before this change via a permissionless sync, and it belongs to the L-24 griefing family. No new exposure.
